messages:
alex: Heads-up: seeing intermittent packet loss between gpu-pool-1 pods in us-west-2 when traffic goes over IPv6. Batch inference jobs show retries and pod-level RDMA errors. Anyone else?

maria: seeing it too — ~5-10% packet loss, east-west latency spikes up to 200-400ms on dual-stack nodes only. IPv4 traffic looks fine.

sam: @alex can you paste a quick traceroute6 and ip -6 route from one affected node to another?

alex: here you go (nodes are gpu-n01 -> gpu-n04):

```
# traceroute -6 -n gpu-n04
traceroute to 2001:db8:10::4 (2001:db8:10::4), 30 hops max, 72 byte packets
 1 2001:db8:10::1 0.3 ms 0.2 ms 0.2 ms
 2 2001:db8:fe::a 0.9 ms 0.7 ms 0.8 ms
 3 2001:db8:spine::2 3.1 ms 3.0 ms 3.1 ms
 4 * * *
 5 * * *

# ip -6 route show
2001:db8:10::/64 dev eth0 proto kernel metric 256 pref medium
2001:db8:0:1::/64 via fe80::abcd:ef12 dev eth1  proto static  metric 100
::/0 via 2001:db8:fe::1 dev eth0  metric 1024
::1/128 via 2001:db8:10::fffe dev eth0  metric 50
```

alex: note the traceroute blackhole at hop 4 and there is a weird /128 host route for ::1 pointing via 2001:db8:10::fffe (that next-hop is not local).

joyce: we pushed the kernel/firmware upgrade to dual-stack nodes last night (kernel 5.15.* + mlx5 fw 22.4). Could be a firmware bug for IPv6 RoCE or an MTU/DF behaviour change.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Finished rolling kernel 5.15.12 -> 5.15.14 to cluster us-west-2-gpu on 1752001200 by ci/pipeline #3829.

sam: I pulled dmesg on one node: saw 'rdma: mlx5_probe: failed to resolve IPv6 address' then later it falls back to IPv4 path in logs. That fallback sends traffic out the general internet NAT path for those pods -> explains misroute and latency.

maria: I captured a tcpdump6 during the spike: saw repeated ICMPv6 "Packet too big" (PTB) messages from ToR, then no fragment reassembly attempts because DF is set. RDMA over IPv6 (RoCEv2) packets were > MTU and getting dropped.

alex: so likely chain: fw/kernel change -> different handling of PMTU/DF for IPv6 -> RDMA/UDP encaps exceeds MTU -> PTB not honoured or path mis-advertised -> traffic falls back or is routed incorrectly.

joyce: hotfix idea: add explicit host routes on the node and on the ToR for the pod /128s and bump MTU to 9000 on the path to avoid fragmentation. Also add nftables rule to allow ICMPv6 PTB through for debugging.

sam: implemented quick host route on gpu-n01: `ip -6 route add 2001:db8:10::/128 dev eth0 via fe80::abcd:ef12` and bumped nic MTU to 9000 in the canary pool.

maria: after the host route + MTU bump the packet loss dropped to ~0.5% and RDMA errors stopped on the canary pods. Traceroute6 now shows no blackhole.

joyce: we should file a vendor ticket on mlx5 fw IPv6 RoCE behaviour and schedule a rollback of the kernel on affected nodes if vendor confirms. Also add a validation in our node rollout job: run IPv6 east-west RDMA smoke test after kernel or fw changes.

alex: created INC-4573 and linked vendor ticket. For now we'll roll the MTU/host route changes cluster-wide for gpu-pools and add route post-install checks to the canary pipeline.

maria: rolling to remaining pools now, watching metrics. will update if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

sam: follow-ups: 1) add route/MTU check to kube-prober e2e, 2) detect unexpected /128 host routes in ip -6 route and alert, 3) document IPv6 RoCE caveats in infra runbook.

alex: thanks all. leaving thread open until next Friday to confirm stability.
